newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire parades Rwandan "prisoners of war".
newsitem.headline: Zaire parades Rwandan "prisoners of war".

text.p: Zaire paraded 10 alleged Rwandan army "prisoners of war" captured in its troubled eastern region and state media urged the army on Monday to hit Rwanda hard.
State television showed the 10 on Sunday night, saying they were seized trying to sabotage the airport at Bukavu, the frontline of fighting between Zaire's army and ethnic Tutsis.

Zaire accuses Tutsi regimes in neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi of arming and even fighting alongside the Banyamulenge Tutsis. Both Rwanda and Burundi deny any involvement in the conflict that has sparked an exodus of refugees from Zaire.
"The 10 regular soldiers of the Rwanda army presented to the public are all Tutsis. They were on a mission to blow up Bukavu airport," the television said.
The announcer referred to the 10, all in civilian clothes, as prisoners of war but did not say when they were seized.
One of the 10 declared on television that he was a Rwandan army soldier.
"We were very tired when we arrived. Zairean soldiers seized us as we slept," he said, speaking in the Kiswahili language widely used in the region.
"We had three types of weapons, including rocket launchers," he added.
In its own report, state radio said four members of the group were of Zairean origin and were fighting with Rwanda to destabilise their country.

A Banyamulenge spokesman in the Rwandan capital Kigali said last week that dissident Zairean groups -- notably Katangese and Kassai people from Zaire's copper belt -- had joined in an offensive to try and overthrow the Kinshasa government.
Rwanda insisted on Monday it was not involved in clashes in Zaire and called on Kinshasa not to expel ethnic Tutsis who have always lived in the country and should be considered Zairean.
The Rwandan government, in a statement issued by its embassy in Brussels, urged Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire not to get involved in violence there and instead return home.

"The government of Rwanda (wants) to inform the Rwandan people and International community it has no part whatsoever in the war and troubles going on between...the armed forces of the Government of Zaire who intend to expel from Zaire the Zairean citizens known as "Banyamulenge", the statement said.
State radio broadcast a jingoistic commentary on Monday, repeating Zairean charges of aggression against Rwanda.

Describing Rwanda as "the frog that wants to play the cow", the Voice of Zaire said: "It is high time the Zaire army used everything at its disposal to put an end to this adventure of destabilisation."
"Zaire must not negotiate before kicking out the invaders," the radio added.

The radio and other state media have been running a similar campaign since Friday. On Monday the radio also turned on the foreign media, accusing the international press of "disseminating erroneous information with the view to discredit the country".
